subject: Starlight integration: SDK handoff, retry/timeout & rate-safety checklist

Alex / Jose — quick technical notes we included in the package (pasted below for immediate use). These are pragmatic defaults we recommend for production at ~50–100 QPS with mixed short/long sequences.

1) SDK auth & sample (Node.js)
```
const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1' });
// streaming generation
const stream = await client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-1.5', prompt: 'Summarize...', max_tokens: 256 });
stream.on('data', (chunk) => process.stdout.write(chunk));
```

2) Recommended runtime config (redwood-config-snippet.txt attached) — key flags:
- batch_size: 8 for mixed-traffic; raise to 16 for high-throughput short queries
- request_timeout_ms: 12000 (12s) for gen endpoints; 6000 for embeddings
- kv_cache_ttl_s: 300 (short-lived cache helps prefix-heavy workloads)
- quant_profile: int8 if quality tolerates it (saves ~2–3x GPU memory)

3) Retry/backoff (client-side):
- On network error or HTTP 5xx: retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff (200ms -> 800ms -> 1600ms).
- On HTTP 429: read "Retry-After" header if present; if absent, backoff with jitter: base 500ms * (2^attempt) + random(0..200ms), cap 8s.
- Idempotency keys: include when retrying non-idempotent calls (especially multi-step tasks).

4) Rate-limit handling & graceful degradation:
- Watch X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset headers we expose.
- For spikes, route non-critical background jobs to lower-cost quantized model variants and preserve interactive UI on a high-priority route.
- Implement client-side smoothing (leaky-bucket) and short client queuing window (~200–400ms) to reduce hotspot bursts.

5) Endpoint migration notes:
- Stage 1: Mirror traffic (send copies) to Redwood hosted; monitor latency & token cost.
- Stage 2: Canary 5–10% for 24–48h; run synthetic prompt suite to validate outputs.
- Failover: keep previous endpoint config as a simple feature-flag rollback.

If you want, we can share a Kubernetes sidecar example for mirroring traffic.

— Vivek
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — super helpful. A couple quick clarifications before our dev sprint on Monday: 
1) Our embeddings calls are typically 128 tokens per request; generation averages 180 tokens. Does your batching guidance change with those numbers?
2) For the canary, can we request a dedicated routing policy (same model, dedicated pool) during our peak payroll run on 9/30? If that's a separate contract, we need to know the procurement lead time.

Also — the SDK zip references a "streaming reconnect" option. Do you recommend client reconnects or server-side fallback for interrupted streams?

— Jose
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com
To: J. Cruz <jc@starlight.io>, Alex Turner <alex@starlight.io>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com, grace_oconnor@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-09-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Starlight integration & SDK onboarding

Jose — answers inline and attached a short checklist (MAP tab: "Technical prechecks").

1) Batching guidance: with 128-token embeddings and ~180-token generation, start with batch_size=8 for gen and 16 for embeddings; monitor latency P95 and increase batch only if P95 < target SLO. We included a small load test script in sdk-samples.zip to help pick the sweet spot.

2) Dedicated routing for 9/30: yes, we can reserve a dedicated pool. Procurement lead time for a short-term dedicated burst is typically 2–3 business days once you sign the request form in HS:52341. I'm copying Grace for SLA and procurement coordination.

3) Streaming reconnects: prefer client-side reconnect with resume token (we include a small resume-token pattern in the SDK). Fallback: server will buffer a short KV window (~5s) but not indefinitely. Pattern we recommend: client attempts a reconnect with exponential backoff up to 10s; if resume fails, fall back to poll-mode or re-issue a short non-streamed generation with same prompt prefix.

Next steps (concrete):
- I'll open HS:52341 with a draft requisition for 9/30 dedicated routing.
- Grace will reach out with the billing/pricing delta and the procurement form.
- Please run the load test script before Mon 9/18 and share results.

Meeting: Thu 9/14 10:00 PT remains on calendar for a technical walkthrough. 

Attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MAP with timeline), sdk-samples.zip (Node & Python samples + load test script), redwood-config-snippet.txt (runtime defaults).

Thanks — we'll keep this thread as the implementation record.

Vanessa Ortiz
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
